kw_outer_court.name: Hornhallow — the Outer Court
kw_outer_court.desc: The old hunting lodge's outer court, cobbled and swept, ringed by burners' shacks, the verderer's post, and the Ironbound's scale-house. Charcoal-smoke sits low most mornings. Every path in Hornhallow starts here.
kw_outer_court.brief: The outer court, ringed by shacks and offices.

variants.desc: The outer court, cobbled and swept. Charcoal-smoke still sits low most mornings, but nobody flinches anymore at a horn carrying from the wood after dark.
The outer court, cobbled and swept. A watch-fire is kept laid year-round now, ready for the one night it's needed, and everyone knows which night that is without being told.
variants.brief: The court, a fire kept ready.

variants.desc: The outer court, cobbled and swept. Some mornings the smoke off the burners' clamps has a different, older smell to it, and nobody in Hornhallow will say what.
variants.brief: The court, and a stranger smoke some mornings.

actions.label: read the guild's charcoal-tally board
fx: Chalked columns: clamps fired, sacks carried, sacks sold to Cinderhall. The Ironbound's count and the guild's own never quite agree, and both sides know it.

kw_kennel_hearth.name: The Kennel Hearth
kw_kennel_hearth.desc: A long hearth-hall built against the old kennel wall, stone still scored where chain-rings once hung. It smells of woodsmoke and, faintly, of dog, though no hound has slept here in four hundred years.
kw_kennel_hearth.brief: The hearth-hall, the old kennel wall behind it.

actions.label: rest by the hearth
fx: You sleep to the tick of the fire and wake stiff but whole. Sabel is already up, turning something over in her hands by the light of the coals.

kw_trade_counter.name: The Packhorse Counter
kw_trade_counter.desc: A plank counter under a lean-to, rope and pitch and traveling gear stacked behind it. Hask trades with whoever comes down off the rides, charcoal-burners and the odd Crown rider alike.
kw_trade_counter.brief: A trade counter, gear stacked behind it.

actions.label: buy a huntsman's boar-spear (9 gold)
fx: Hask hands it over crossways, the old way. "Broad head, cross-bar so it doesn't run through and lose you your grip. Someone's hunt spear, once."

actions.label: buy a twist of dried venison (3 gold)
fx: Hask weighs it once, out of habit, and wraps it in oiled cloth. "Off the wood, same as everything else here."

kw_verderer_post.name: The Verderer's Post
kw_verderer_post.desc: A narrow office of Crown timber, a felling-warrant pinned flat under glass on the desk, its seal unbroken. Maps of the ridings cover one whole wall, every oak worth felling already marked in red.
kw_verderer_post.brief: The verderer's office, a warrant under glass.

kw_weigh_house.name: The Ironbound Weigh-House
kw_weigh_house.desc: A stone scale-house, the Ironbound's own beam-scale bolted to the floor. Sacked charcoal is stacked to the rafters on one side, empty floor waiting on the other — floor enough, the factor likes to say, for the whole wood.
kw_weigh_house.brief: The weigh-house, a beam-scale bolted down.

kw_charcoal_yard.name: The Charcoal-Master's Yard
kw_charcoal_yard.desc: A working yard, three clamps smoking under their turf in slow relay, cordwood stacked in ricks head-high. Everything here is black-handed and practical, down to the guild's own brass scale, weighed twice a day.
kw_charcoal_yard.brief: The yard, clamps smoking under turf.

kw_woodward_cot.name: The Woodward's Cot
kw_woodward_cot.desc: A one-room cot at the wood's edge, old ride-maps curling on every wall, chalk-marks for boundaries nobody living set. Hollis keeps it as bare as a Keeper's cell, though he'd never call himself one outright.
kw_woodward_cot.brief: The woodward's cot, old maps on the walls.

kw_hunt_chapel.name: The Hunt's Chapel
kw_hunt_chapel.desc: A small chapel gone half to ruin, roof open to the sky over the old nave, a huntsman's saint carved crude above the door. Father Twyne keeps what's left of it, sweeping leaves off a floor nobody else visits.
kw_hunt_chapel.brief: The ruined chapel, a huntsman's saint over the door.

kw_ride_gate.name: The Ride-Gate
kw_ride_gate.desc: The last gate before the ridings proper, its timbers scarred by four hundred years of charcoal-carts. Past it the wood closes in fast, and the light changes the way it does before rain.
kw_ride_gate.brief: The last gate before the ridings.

variants.desc: The last gate before the ridings. Beyond it, stumps show pale where the verderer's marked oaks have already come down, cart-ruts cut fresh and deep toward Marrowgate's road.
variants.brief: The gate. Fresh stumps show beyond it.

variants.desc: The last gate before the ridings. Beyond it the wood stands thinner every season, coppice-cuts spreading outward from the gate in a slow, deliberate ring toward Cinderhall.
variants.brief: The gate. Coppice-cuts spread beyond it.

variants.desc: The last gate before the ridings, standing open the way it always has. Nothing beyond it has changed, which out here counts for a great deal.
variants.brief: The gate. Unchanged beyond it, and glad of it.

kw_south_track.name: The South Track
kw_south_track.desc: The ridings narrow and straighten here, running south toward bare downs and a smudge of forge-smoke on the horizon. Behind you the wood closes ranks again, oak and holly, dense as a shut door.
kw_south_track.brief: The south track, downs on the horizon.
onEnterOnce: This is the Kingswood: the old royal hunting forest under the Spine, where a king's hunt rode out four hundred years ago and never came home.

kw_east_track.name: The East Track
kw_east_track.desc: The ridings thin here, oak giving slowly over to open heather. East, the trees fall away into Wardmoor's wide gray moor; behind you the Kingswood shuts close again, dense and watchful.
kw_east_track.brief: The east track, moor opening beyond it.
onEnterOnce: This is the Kingswood: the old royal hunting forest under the Spine, where a king's hunt rode out four hundred years ago and never came home.

kw_boar_spear.name: a huntsman's boar-spear
kw_boar_spear.hint: broad-headed, cross-barred; a step above a belt-knife

kw_dried_venison.name: a twist of dried venison
kw_dried_venison.hint: off the wood; eat it to ease a wound

fx: Tough going, well salted, and it sits well enough. The ache eases before you've finished chewing.
